boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Army of the Tennessee and the Army of Vicksburg without counts; the live field reads zero. Greene gives about 20,000 effective defenders when the siege began, 40,000 Union infantry present for duty on May 22, and Grant's army at 71,141 men and 248 guns on June 30; by late June the garrison's returns showed nearly 22,000, with about 7,000 in the hospitals. Pemberton says the garrison held out against an enemy five times its number.
claims.rationale: Figures at different dates and scopes; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says Vicksburg surrendered on July 4 after prolonged siege operations; Pemberton says the garrison was surrendered at 10 a.m.; Greene says 29,391 were paroled, 790 refused parole, and the force surrendered was about 31,000, with 172 guns.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's statements about the Confederacy being split and Grant's reputation are campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 19,233 total (US 10,142; CS 9,091); the live field reads 37532 total (US 4835; CS 32697;). Greene says Grant's losses in the entire campaign, including the Jackson expedition, were a little less than 10,000, and that about 31,000 surrendered.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Greene's campaign-wide Union figure spans other frozen engagements and must not be assigned to the siege; the live Confederate figure appears to include the surrendered garrison. No figure is adopted.

open_questions: Grant's, the corps commanders' and the Confederate division reports, Johnston's siege correspondence and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
